title: BOX OF VINTAGE BOOKS INCL 1860
findings: Photos show 4 books, not a full box: (1) 'Engineer's, Architect's and Contractor's Pocket Book for 1860', black pebbled leather wallet-style pocket book with gilt title, supports the 1860 claim (an annual Victorian technical pocket book/diary, publisher not visible); (2) 'Trautwine' in gilt on maroon limp leather, i.e. Trautwine's Civil Engineer's Pocket-Book (edition and date not visible, in a plastic sleeve); (3) ivory/celluloid-style prize binding with embossed Normanhurst 1882 'Strive & Thrive' crest, prize label inside reads 'Dorothy Malcolm PRIZE For Earnest Work Form Lower VI Christmas 1912' (Normanhurst School, Sydney), title not shown; (4) black pebbled leather book with yapp-ish edges, no title visible (probably a Bible or prayer book). Edges of a red book and an orange-edged book also intrude at the photo margin, unreadable. Titles of books 3 and 4 not readable.
condition: 1860 pocket book: worn and scuffed leather, corners and edges rubbed through, two pin/tack holes or punctures on front cover. Trautwine: rubbed and faded. Prize binding: ivory boards a little yellowed, spine edge worn. Black leather book: rubbed edges and corners.
reason: Genuine 1860 engineer's pocket book plus Trautwine and a 1912 Normanhurst prize binding; 19th-century technical items with a modest specialist market.
marks_read: Engineer's Architect's and Contractor's Pocket Book for 1860; Trautwine; Normanhurst 1882 Strive & Thrive; prize label Dorothy Malcolm Christmas 1912
